newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Italian 98 deficit below three percent - Ciampi.
newsitem.headline: Italian 98 deficit below three percent - Ciampi.

text.p: Italy's Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi repeated on Monday that Italy would reduce its budget deficit to three percent of gross domestic product in 1997 and announced he was aiming to reduce it to below that level in 1998.

Ciampi, who was accompanied at a meeting of EU finance ministers by finance minister Vincenzo Visco, played down reports that the Commission was sending Rome an ultimatum to put its finances in order.
"Together with minister Visco we have not come to Brussels for a duel because there is no reason for a duel," he said.
"The state of our relations with Brussels is clear. They recognise that we are making an enormous effort."

He added that Italy would be discussing in the next two weeks a pluriannual economic and finance programme updating its efforts to qualify for the single currency and the plan would be forwarded to Brussels early in June.

Asked whether the programme would foresee a budget deficit below three percent in 1998 to show Italy's commitment to durable and sustainable sound finance, he said: "Yes it will be below three percent."
The European Commission forecast last month that Italy's deficit would stand at 3.2 percent in 1997 and 3.9 percent in 1998.
